dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a matrix-norm package on n by n real matrices, this is its real-valued evaluation function.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It evaluates the algorithm's matrix norm on the total error matrix in the conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: This dependent inductive type packages an admissible data family for an algorithm and dimension, with the fields and assumptions supplied by D012.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The universal family binder ranges only over these admissible packages; its exact matrices, perturbations, inherited errors, and embedded estimates determine the target bound.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: The subtype of real numbers epsilon satisfying 0 < epsilon.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Every epsilon in the proposition is strictly positive, and epsilon.val is its underlying real value.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: This inductive type packages an algorithm as described by D015: dimension-indexed matrix norms, a nonnegative growth-controlled function mu, and a matrix-valued product operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The proposition is universal over such algorithm packages and uses their norm, mu value, and product operation.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: The first field of an algorithm package, assigning a matrix-norm package to every natural dimension.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: At dimension n it supplies the norm N_n used on the total error and throughout the bound.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006
dependency_coverage.meaning: For epsilon, it is the algorithmic product of the perturbed inputs minus the exact matrix product of the unperturbed matrices.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: This is the total error matrix whose norm is bounded in the conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef007
dependency_coverage.meaning: For epsilon, it is mu(n) epsilon N_n(A) N_n(B) + N_n(A) e_R(epsilon) + e_L(epsilon) N_n(B), where A and B are the exact matrices and e_L and e_R are the inherited-error functions.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the explicitly retained first-order and inherited-error part of the right-hand side, before adding the existential quadratic remainder.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef008
dependency_coverage.meaning: An inductive package representing a norm-like function on n by n real matrices, with the norm axioms supplied by D019.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The algorithm provides one such package in each dimension, and its value field is used as N_n.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef009
dependency_coverage.meaning: The second field of a family package, namely its exact left n by n real matrix A.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: A appears in the exact product AB and in the factors N_n(A) on the right-hand side.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef010
dependency_coverage.meaning: The third field of a family package, namely its exact right n by n real matrix B.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: B appears in the exact product AB and in the factors N_n(B) on the right-hand side.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef011
dependency_coverage.meaning: The sixth field of a family package, a nonnegative real-valued left inherited-error function e_L on positive epsilon.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It contributes the term e_L(epsilon) N_n(B) to the target bound.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef012
dependency_coverage.meaning: The family constructor requires 0 < n; exact matrices A and B; perturbations Delta_A and Delta_B; nonnegative inherited errors e_L and e_R; nonnegative coefficients c_L, c_R, and C_0; and a radius rho_0 > 0. It requires N_n(Delta_A(epsilon)) <= e_L(epsilon) and N_n(Delta_B(epsilon)) <= e_R(epsilon) for every positive epsilon, e_L(epsilon) <= c_L epsilon and e_R(epsilon) <= c_R epsilon when epsilon <= rho_0, and N_n(P(epsilon,A+Delta_A,B+Delta_B) - (A+Delta_A)(B+Delta_B)) <= mu(n) epsilon N_n(A) N_n(B) + C_0 epsilon^2 when epsilon <= rho_0.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: These conditions are embedded in the type of the universally quantified family. They provide the local input-error and algorithmic-error assumptions from which the asserted total-error estimate can hold.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef013
dependency_coverage.meaning: The seventh field of a family package, a nonnegative real-valued right inherited-error function e_R on positive epsilon.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It contributes the term N_n(A) e_R(epsilon) to the target bound.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef014
dependency_coverage.meaning: For n, this is the type of n by n matrices over the real numbers, indexed by Fin n in both coordinates.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: All exact matrices, perturbations, algorithm outputs, products, and error matrices have this type.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef015
dependency_coverage.meaning: The algorithm constructor takes a matrix norm N_n for each n, a function mu with mu(n) >= 0, a natural degree d, a constant K >= 0 satisfying mu(n) <= K n^d for every positive n, and a product operation P mapping n, positive epsilon, and two n by n matrices to an n by n matrix.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It restricts the algorithm binder to such packages. The conclusion directly uses N_n, mu(n), and P, while the polynomial growth data are only indirect type-level restrictions.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef016
dependency_coverage.meaning: The second field of an algorithm package, namely the real-valued function mu on natural dimensions.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Its value mu(n) multiplies epsilon N_n(A) N_n(B) in the leading term.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef017
dependency_coverage.meaning: Ordinary multiplication of two n by n real matrices, with entries formed by finite dot products.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It defines both the exact product AB subtracted in the total error and the exact products of perturbed inputs used in family assumptions.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef018
dependency_coverage.meaning: The algorithm's product operation applied at epsilon to A + Delta_A(epsilon) and B + Delta_B(epsilon).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the computed matrix output appearing in the total error.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef019
dependency_coverage.meaning: The matrix-norm constructor packages a function N with N(A) >= 0, N(A) = 0 iff A = 0, N(cA) = |c|N(A), N(A+B) <= N(A)+N(B), and N(AB) <= N(A)N(B).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It ensures every algorithm norm used in the proposition is definite, absolutely homogeneous, subadditive, and submultiplicative.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef020
dependency_coverage.meaning: The fourth field of a family package, the left perturbation Delta_A(epsilon).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is added to A before the algorithm's product is evaluated.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef021
dependency_coverage.meaning: The fifth field of a family package, the right perturbation Delta_B(epsilon).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is added to B before the algorithm's product is evaluated.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef022
dependency_coverage.meaning: The eighth field of an algorithm package, its product operation P(n,epsilon,X,Y).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It produces the computed product used in the total error and in the family's local algorithmic-error assumption.

dependency_coverage.name: And
dependency_coverage.meaning: Logical conjunction of two propositions.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It requires the quadratic coefficient to be nonnegative together with the remaining existence claim, and requires the radius to be positive together with the universal estimate.

dependency_coverage.name: Exists
dependency_coverage.meaning: Existential quantification over values satisfying a predicate.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It introduces the real quadratic coefficient and, inside it, the real radius.

dependency_coverage.name: HAdd.hAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: Typeclass-selected heterogeneous addition; at all direct target occurrences it resolves to ordinary real addition.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It adds the leading error expression and the quadratic term, and combines the three terms defining D007.

dependency_coverage.name: HMul.hMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: Typeclass-selected heterogeneous multiplication; at direct target occurrences it resolves to ordinary real multiplication.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It forms the products in the leading term and the product of the existential coefficient with epsilon squared.

dependency_coverage.name: HPow.hPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: Typeclass-selected exponentiation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With a real base and natural exponent 2, it forms epsilon squared.

dependency_coverage.name: LE.le
dependency_coverage.meaning: The typeclass-selected non-strict order relation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For reals it expresses nonnegativity, epsilon <= radius, and the final norm upper bound.

dependency_coverage.name: LT.lt
dependency_coverage.meaning: The typeclass-selected strict order relation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For reals it defines positive epsilon and requires the existential radius to be positive.

dependency_coverage.name: Monoid.toNatPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: Natural-number exponentiation induced by a monoid's repeated multiplication operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the standard real natural power used to interpret epsilon^2.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat
dependency_coverage.meaning: The type of natural numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the universally quantified matrix dimension n and the exponent 2; it also occurs in packaged growth data.

dependency_coverage.name: OfNat.ofNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: Interpretation of a natural numeral in a type possessing the corresponding OfNat instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets 0 as a real number and 2 as a natural exponent.

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.meaning: The type of real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Norm values, epsilon values, coefficients, radii, inherited errors, and matrix entries are real.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: Ordinary addition on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines the additions in the right-hand side of the target inequality.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLE
dependency_coverage.meaning: The usual non-strict order on real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the mathematical meanings of C >= 0, epsilon <= r, and the final <= inequality.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLT
dependency_coverage.meaning: The usual strict order on real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the meanings of epsilon > 0 and r > 0.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: The multiplicative monoid structure on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies repeated multiplication for the real square epsilon^2.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: Ordinary multiplication on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines all scalar products in the target bound.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instZero
dependency_coverage.meaning: The zero element of the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the zero used in positivity and nonnegativity conditions.

dependency_coverage.name: Subtype.val
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projection from an element of a subtype to its underlying value.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It extracts the real epsilon from the proof-carrying positive-real epsilon.

dependency_coverage.name: Zero.toOfNat0
dependency_coverage.meaning: The canonical interpretation of the numeral 0 from a type's zero element.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It ensures every displayed real zero is the ordinary additive zero.

dependency_coverage.name: instHAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: The homogeneous HAdd instance induced by an ordinary Add instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes HAdd on reals coincide with ordinary real addition.

dependency_coverage.name: instHMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: The homogeneous HMul instance induced by an ordinary Mul instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes HMul on reals coincide with ordinary real multiplication.

dependency_coverage.name: instHPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: The homogeneous HPow instance induced by a Pow instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the target's heterogeneous power notation use ordinary real natural powers.

dependency_coverage.name: instOfNatNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: The canonical OfNat instance interpreting a natural numeral n as the natural number n itself.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets the exponent numeral 2 as the natural number two.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin
dependency_coverage.meaning: For n, the finite type of natural indices strictly below n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It indexes the rows and columns of every n by n matrix.

dependency_coverage.name: HSub.hSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: Typeclass-selected heterogeneous subtraction.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For matrices it forms computed output minus exact product in the error matrices.

dependency_coverage.name: Matrix.sub
dependency_coverage.meaning: Pointwise subtraction of matrices, inherited from subtraction of their entries.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the error matrix equal entrywise to the computed matrix minus the exact matrix product.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: Ordinary subtraction on real numbers, defined as addition of the additive inverse.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It induces pointwise subtraction for real matrices.

dependency_coverage.name: Subtype
dependency_coverage.meaning: The type of values equipped with a proof that they satisfy a predicate.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It represents epsilon as a real number equipped with a proof of strict positivity.

dependency_coverage.name: instHSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: The homogeneous HSub instance induced by an ordinary Sub instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes matrix HSub coincide with ordinary pointwise matrix subtraction.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin.fintype
dependency_coverage.meaning: The finite enumeration structure on Fin n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It permits the finite sums over inner indices used in n by n matrix multiplication.

dependency_coverage.name: Matrix
dependency_coverage.meaning: A matrix with row type m, column type n, and entries in alpha is a function m -> n -> alpha.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Specialized to Fin n and Real, it is the ambient type of all matrices in the proposition.

dependency_coverage.name: Matrix.add
dependency_coverage.meaning: Pointwise addition of matrices.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It forms A + Delta_A(epsilon) and B + Delta_B(epsilon).

dependency_coverage.name: Matrix.instHMulOfFintypeOfMulOfAddCommMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: Matrix multiplication defined by finite dot products over the shared index type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the ordinary exact matrix products used by D017.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat.cast
dependency_coverage.meaning: The canonical cast of a natural number into a type with a NatCast structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets n as a real number in the polynomial growth restriction on mu; it does not occur directly in the final inequality.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAddCommMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: The additive commutative monoid structure of the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies zero and finite summation of real products for matrix multiplication.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instNatCast
dependency_coverage.meaning: The canonical embedding of natural numbers into the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the real value of n in the algorithm package's growth bound mu(n) <= K n^d.

dependency_coverage.name: instLTNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: The usual strict order on natural numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets the embedded family requirement 0 < n and the positive-dimension condition in the growth bound.

dependency_coverage.name: Algebra.id
dependency_coverage.meaning: The identity algebra structure of a commutative semiring over itself.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For the reals it supports the standard scalar action used in the matrix norm's absolute-homogeneity axiom.

dependency_coverage.name: Algebra.toSMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: The scalar-multiplication structure supplied by an algebra.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes real scalar multiplication available for real matrices in the norm package.

dependency_coverage.name: CommSemiring.toSemiring
dependency_coverage.meaning: The semiring structure inherited from a commutative semiring.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supports the identity real algebra and hence the scalar multiplication used indirectly by the norm axioms.

dependency_coverage.name: Eq
dependency_coverage.meaning: Propositional equality between two values of the same type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It expresses definiteness of the matrix norm through N(A) = 0 iff A is the zero matrix.

dependency_coverage.name: HSMul.hSMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: Typeclass-selected heterogeneous scalar multiplication.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It denotes multiplication of a matrix by a real scalar in the matrix norm's homogeneity axiom.

dependency_coverage.name: Iff
dependency_coverage.meaning: Logical equivalence between two propositions.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It states the two-way definiteness condition N(A) = 0 iff A = 0 in the norm package.

dependency_coverage.name: Matrix.smul
dependency_coverage.meaning: Pointwise scalar multiplication of matrices.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It realizes the scalar multiple cA appearing in the norm homogeneity axiom.

dependency_coverage.name: Matrix.zero
dependency_coverage.meaning: The pointwise zero matrix.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the zero matrix used in the norm definiteness axiom.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAddGroup
dependency_coverage.meaning: The additive group structure of the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It provides negation needed for real absolute value in the norm homogeneity axiom.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instCommSemiring
dependency_coverage.meaning: The commutative semiring structure of the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supports the identity algebra and standard real scalar action used indirectly by matrix scalar multiplication.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.lattice
dependency_coverage.meaning: The lattice order structure of the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supports the maximum operation used to define real absolute value.

dependency_coverage.name: abs
dependency_coverage.meaning: In an ordered additive group, abs(c) is the maximum of c and -c; for reals this is ordinary absolute value.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It appears in the matrix norm axiom N(cA) = |c|N(A).

dependency_coverage.name: instHSMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: The HSMul instance induced by an ordinary scalar-multiplication structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes heterogeneous real-matrix scalar multiplication coincide with the standard pointwise scalar action.

binders: An implicit natural number n, universally quantified.
An algorithm package, universally quantified, containing dimension-indexed matrix norms N_m, a function mu, associated growth data, and a matrix product operation P.

An admissible family for that algorithm at dimension n, universally quantified and carrying exact matrices A and B, perturbations Delta_A and Delta_B, inherited-error functions e_L and e_R, and the assumptions described below.
A real second-order coefficient C, existentially chosen after n, the algorithm, and the family.
A real radius r, existentially chosen inside the choice of C.
A positive real epsilon, universally quantified inside the local implication after C and r are chosen.
hypotheses: Each N_m is nonnegative, definite, absolutely homogeneous, subadditive, and submultiplicative on m by m real matrices.
The algorithm package has mu(m) >= 0 for every m and stores a natural degree d and K >= 0 such that mu(m) <= K m^d for every m > 0.
For every positive epsilon, e_L(epsilon) >= 0, e_R(epsilon) >= 0, N_n(Delta_A(epsilon)) <= e_L(epsilon), and N_n(Delta_B(epsilon)) <= e_R(epsilon).
The family stores nonnegative c_L and c_R and a radius rho_0 > 0 such that, whenever epsilon <= rho_0, e_L(epsilon) <= c_L epsilon and e_R(epsilon) <= c_R epsilon.

The family stores C_0 >= 0 such that, whenever epsilon <= rho_0, N_n(P(n,epsilon,A+Delta_A(epsilon),B+Delta_B(epsilon)) - (A+Delta_A(epsilon))(B+Delta_B(epsilon))) <= mu(n) epsilon N_n(A) N_n(B) + C_0 epsilon^2.
conclusions: There exists a real C with C >= 0; C may depend on n, the algorithm package, and the entire family.
For that C there exists a real r with r > 0; r may also depend on C and all earlier binders.
For every positive real epsilon with epsilon <= r, N_n(P(n,epsilon,A+Delta_A(epsilon),B+Delta_B(epsilon)) - AB) <= mu(n) epsilon N_n(A) N_n(B) + N_n(A)e_R(epsilon) + e_L(epsilon)N_n(B) + C epsilon^2.
mathematical_definitions: M_n(R) denotes the n by n real matrices, with ordinary matrix addition, subtraction, scalar multiplication, and multiplication.
N_n(X) is the value of the algorithm's norm package in dimension n.
P(n,epsilon,X,Y) is the matrix returned by the algorithm's abstract product operation on X and Y at positive parameter epsilon.
A and B are the family's exact left and right matrices; Delta_A(epsilon) and Delta_B(epsilon) are their epsilon-dependent perturbations.
E(epsilon) = P(n,epsilon,A+Delta_A(epsilon),B+Delta_B(epsilon)) - AB is the total error against the unperturbed exact product.
L(epsilon) = mu(n) epsilon N_n(A) N_n(B) + N_n(A)e_R(epsilon) + e_L(epsilon)N_n(B) is the explicitly retained leading error expression.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every natural dimension n, every admissible algorithm package, and every admissible family at that dimension, there are a nonnegative real constant C and a positive real radius r such that every positive epsilon no larger than r satisfies N_n(P(n,epsilon,A+Delta_A(epsilon),B+Delta_B(epsilon)) - AB) <= mu(n) epsilon N_n(A) N_n(B) + N_n(A)e_R(epsilon) + e_L(epsilon)N_n(B) + C epsilon^2.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: Epsilon ranges only over strictly positive reals; the proposition says nothing directly at epsilon = 0 or for negative epsilon.
The estimate is local: no bound is asserted for epsilon greater than the existentially chosen radius r.
The coefficient C and radius r are not uniform across dimensions, algorithms, or families and may depend on all preceding data; no explicit formula, minimum, or uniqueness is asserted.
The target coefficient C and radius r are not required to equal the family's stored local coefficient C_0 and radius rho_0.
Under the supplied constructor inventory, every family contains a proof that n > 0, so the outer universal statement at n = 0 is vacuous because there is no constructible family at that dimension.

The theorem applies only to algorithm and family packages satisfying the strong embedded norm, growth, perturbation, inherited-error, and local product-error assumptions; it is not a statement about arbitrary matrix-valued operations.
The inherited errors e_L and e_R are upper bounds for perturbation norms and need not equal those norms.
The result is only a norm upper bound. It does not assert an equality, lower bound, asymptotic limit, sharp coefficient, or convergence statement.
No concrete computational or rounding semantics for P are encoded beyond the package assumptions, and the polynomial growth data for mu do not appear directly in the final local inequality.
